prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation; automation = bay control, station coordination, external interfaces; supervisory/bay/protection layers separated, loss never silently substituted. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper): validates requests vs local mode, interlocks, authority, availability before bay outputs; compares returned indications to requested state, flags incomplete/contradictory operation; receives Breaker Inspection Tag (links equipment context to authorized record); stale points to degraded state; timestamps; produces Bay Status Digest to Glasswing. North/South Bay Controllers: separate scopes, no substitution; block unready close; North keeps local control in approved mode if supervisory comms lost; South reports local mode/availability. Breaker Control Unit: authoritative interlocks; executes accepted commands; returns position/circuit-health indications. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem): independent trips, no supervisory dependence; produces Relay Diagnostic Note to Larkspur. North Protection Panel: zone logic, independent trip paths. Transformer Protection Panel: transformer protection, reports abnormal conditions. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing): controls/indications to authorized personnel; shows quality/stale status; retains alarms; produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip. Station Gateway: brokers authorized traffic, carries indications with quality/timestamps; rejects and logs malformed/stale/unauthorized requests; reports link/protocol errors, never as equipment-state change; produces Protocol Retry Summary. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin): quality-checked time reference; Clock Drift Snapshot to Orchard; holdover. Sequence Event Archive (Orchard): authoritative time-tagged changes/control outcomes, audited, retention/holds/backup. Engineering Workstation: config review only, not operating commands; produces Settings Review Receipt. Maintenance Remote Terminal: authorized sessions, no interlock bypass. Station DC System: monitored control/protection supply; loss = abnormal alarm; produces Battery Load Test Record. Actors: Control Room Operator: commands only via procedures/Glasswing; switching requests to Keystone; acknowledges after review; cleared ≠ fixed; produces Clearance Handoff Memo; verifies consistency after handback. Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone): produces Isolation Boundary Card; confirms handback. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur): reviews protection events/settings coordination. Substation Field Crew (Cinder): confirms identity/conditions; sends Breaker Inspection Tag. Substation Supervisor: escalation, exceptional switching. Requirements: hold/stop points; local precedence; unique revisions; no copied-value approval; pre-deploy checks; work windows.

Document units:
S195: Substation Supervisor ensures communication changes, point mapping changes, and control logic changes are managed through station change control.
S196: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S197: Maintenance windows are planned around feeder loading, switching constraints, and the availability of qualified personnel.
S198: The Substation Supervisor coordinates work timing with the Switching Desk Coordinator and confirms that operating responsibilities are understood.
S199: The Control Room Operator reviews the equipment affected by each work package and identifies any required operating restrictions.
S200: The Switching Desk Coordinator confirms switching prerequisites before field work begins and keeps the approved switching sequence current.
S201: Substation Field Crew performs work only after required clearances, isolation, and grounding have been confirmed through established procedures.
S202: Work boundaries are verified locally before personnel approach exposed conductors or operate equipment under maintenance.
S203: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews test scope, approved settings, and restoration criteria before protection testing starts.
S204: Testing is performed with approved procedures, calibrated instruments, and a defined means of stopping the test if unexpected indications occur.
S205: The Engineering Workstation is used for authorized configuration review, and changes are applied only through station change control.
S206: The Maintenance Remote Terminal uses the review receipt to support controlled maintenance review.
S207: The Bay Automation Controller uses the load test record to support maintenance review.
S208: The Station Supervisory Control System receives the Protocol Retry Summary for operational review.
S209: Cinder verifies that field work remains within the approved work boundary and reports any unsafe condition through established channels.
S210: Orchard retains event information needed to review testing and restoration activity.
S211: Feeder Protection Relay testing is coordinated so that protection coverage is not unintentionally removed from an energized feeder.
S212: A protection function placed out of service is tracked by the responsible operator until it is restored and verified.
S213: The Breaker Control Unit is tested using controlled commands that cannot bypass local interlocks or approved operating authority.
S214: Remote commands are inhibited when equipment status is uncertain or when required permissives are unavailable.
S215: If communications are degraded, the Control Room Operator treats remote indications as unavailable until their reliability is established.
S216: Substation Field Crew verifies equipment indications locally when remote status is uncertain and reports discrepancies through established operating channels.
S217: Manual operation is permitted only under approved procedures and with the required local checks and communication with the Control Room Operator.
